AWARD/JUDGMENT FACTUAL POSITION AND PLEADINGS 1.

The present petition was filed on 21.04.2016 seeking compensation to the tune of Rs. 10,00,000/-
in respect of injuries sustained by Sh. Mayank Aggarwal S/o Sh. Om Prakash
LOVLEEN

2023.04.21 (hereinafter referred to as "petitioner") in a road traffic accident which took place on 15/05/2014 at about 12:15 PM at a spot situated near Sindhi Park, Old Rajinder Nagar, Delhi.

As per this petition, the petitioner was riding a scooter bearing registration no. DL-14-SC-8065 and was travelling to Kotak Mahindra Bank, Old Rajinder Nagar, Delhi and when he reached at the spot of accident, the driver of the vehicle bearing registration no. DL- 3CBD-6886 (hereinafter referred to as "offending vehicle") suddenly opened the door of the same.
Due to above act and conduct of the driver of the offending vehicle, petitioner collided with the offending vehicle and sustained injuries.
Petitioner was immediately removed to Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, Delhi.
An FIR no. 221/14 PS Rajinder Nagar U/s 337 IPC was registered against the driver of the offending vehicle at the instance of the petitioner.

As per petition, the petitioner has spent a sum of Rs. 1,25,000/- towards medical treatment and also sustained financial losses to the tune of Rs. 1,50,000/- as he remained bed- ridden for quite sometime.
Petitioner further claims that he had sustained 100% permanent disability as he lost his great toe due to the above accident.
R-1 is stated to be the driver-cum-owner of the offending vehicle.
R-2 is stated to be the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Notice of this petition was issued to both the respondents.
2. A Written Statement was filed by R-1 wherein she claims that no negligence is attributable to her as the offending vehicle was undergoing repair in the service lane at the relevant time.
Rather, it is claimed that at the relevant time the petitioner was riding his scooter at a high speed and therefore he sustained LOVLEEN Date: 2023.04.21 injuries on account of his own fault.
Averments of the petitioner have been denied in toto.
3. A Written Statement was filed by the R-2/ Insurance company wherein averments made by the petitioner have been denied in toto.
However, it is admitted that at the relevant time, the offending vehicle was covered by an insurance policy issued by itself in favour of R-1.

It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.

sentences.text: As already discussed above, the petitioner examined himself as PW-1 in order to prove the factual averments regarding the occurrence of accident.
PW-1 has clearly and categorically stated that at the relevant date, time and place he was riding his scooter when R-1 suddenly opened the door of the offending vehicle, leading to a collision.
He further deposed that he sustained grievous injuries because of the said collision.
The above oral testimony of PW-1 has gone unchallenged and unrebutted qua R-1 as she did not bother to cross-examine PW- 1.
PW-1 was cross
- examined in brief on behalf of R-2/ Insurance Company but the same does not reflect any inconsistency or infirmity at all.
In fact, Ld. Counsel for R-2/ Insurance Company fairly conceded the occurrence of accident and its manner during the course of final arguments.

As such,
this Tribunal finds it appropriate to hold that oral testimony of PW-1 is reliable, trustworthy and worth acting upon.

10. The very fact that R-1 has already been charge- sheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 338 IPC in LOVLEEN Date:
the above criminal case/FIR in itself is a strong circumstance to support the above oral testimony of PW1 and the case of petitioner on this issue.

The copies of FIR,
Charge-sheet, Mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle and discharge summary of the petitioner also corroborate the oral testimony of PW1.

11. Besides the above, R-1 himself was the best witness who could have stepped into the witness box to challenge the depositions being made by PW1 regarding the above accident and its manner etc.,
but she has not done so.

Therefore, an adverse inference on this aspect is also required to be drawn against the respondents in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.

"Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?"

16 . As the issue no.1 has been proved in affirmative and in favour of the petitioner, the petitioner has become entitled to be compensated for the injuries suffered in the above accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
17. In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MV Act the compensation which is to be awarded by this tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. pecuniary as well as non-pecuniary damages.
The pecuniary damages or LOVLEEN Date:

special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which he had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by him in the accident.
The non-pecuniary or general damages are those damages which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

The pecuniary or special damages generally include the expenses incurred by the claimant towards his treatment, special diet, conveyance, cost of nursing/ attendant, loss of income/earning capacity etc. and the non- pecuniary damages generally include the compensation for the mental or physical shock, pain and sufferings, loss of amenities of life, marriage prospects and disfiguration etc.
The above categories falling under both the heads of compensation are not exhaustive in nature but only illustrative.

It is also necessary to state here that no amount of money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the same position or place where he was before the accident and an effort is to be made only to reasonably compensate him or to put him almost in the same place or position where he could have been if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The object of compensating him is also not to reward him or to make him rich in an unjust manner.

(i) Medical or Treatment Expenses 19.
The petitioner has placed on judicial file his original medical treatment records/ medical bills as Mark A to Mark F, Ex. PW1/10 & Ex. PW1/11, Ex. PW1/13, Mark G to Mark I and PW4/1(Colly).

As per the said documents, petitioner has incurred medical expenses to the tune of Rs. 60,020.62/.

In the absence of any contest to the said documents (placed on record by the petitioner), the petitioner is held entitled to an amount of Rs. 60,020/ (rounded off) under this head.
(ii) Loss of actual earnings 21.

In his affidavit Ex. PW1/A, the petitioner states that he suffered financial loss to the tune of Rs.
1,50,000/- as he remained bed-ridden from 15/04/2014 to 20/08/2014.

However, he has failed to specify his vocation/ employment or his monthly Digitally signed by LOVLEEN LOVLEEN Date:

Only a salary certificate Ex.
PW1/25 has been placed on record by petitioner, as per which petitioner was employed as a 'Sales Executive' in Aman Financial Services and was paid Rs. 15,000/-
as salary in cash.
But the said document could not be relied upon as petitioner has not bothered to examine the person who issued the said certificate.

In the facts and circumstances, it would be appropriate to assume the monthly earnings of the petitioner as per the minimum wages payable to an unskilled person in Delhi (petitioner being an ordinary resident of Delhi as per DAR) as on the date of accident.
As per relevant notification, the minimum wages admissible to an unskilled person as on 15.05.2014 in Delhi were Rs. 8,554/-.

In view of the medical records Ex.
PW4/1(Colly), it would not be inappropriate to assume that the petitioner would not have been able to resume his work/ employment for a period of 03 months at least.
As such, the petitioner is held entitled to a sum of Rs. 25,662/- (Rs. 8,554/- X 3).
The said sum is awarded to the petitioner under this head.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.
The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.

Admittedly, R- 1 has not explained the circumstances under which she suddenly opened the door of her vehicle (i.e. the offending vehicle)
leading to a collision with the petitioner's scooter at the relevant time.
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. pecuniary as well as non-pecuniary damages.
special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which he had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by him in the accident.
The pecuniary or special damages generally include the expenses incurred by the claimant towards his treatment, special diet, conveyance, cost of nursing/ attendant, loss of income/earning capacity etc. and the non- pecuniary damages generally include the compensation for the mental or physical shock, pain and sufferings, loss of amenities of life, marriage prospects and disfiguration etc.
The above categories falling under both the heads of compensation are not exhaustive in nature but only illustrative.
It is also necessary to state here that no amount of money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the same position or place where he was before the accident and an effort is to be made only to reasonably compensate him or to put him almost in the same place or position where he could have been if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The object of compensating him is also not to reward him or to make him rich in an unjust manner.
